newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge, union explore resuming talks.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge, union explore resuming talks.

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd and its striking Sudbury, Ontario workers are exploring whether contract talks can resume later this week, a union official said on Tuesday.
Union and company negotiators have not met since about 1,400 workers walked off the job last Friday.
"Right now we're exploring whether or not discussions will be held this week," Rolly Gauthier, Local 598 president of the Canadian Auto Workers union, said in a telephone interview on Tuesday.
"The calls have been put in today," Gauthier said.
Falconbridge officials were unavailable for comment.
Falconbridge's Sudbury operations last year produced 45,700 metric tons of nickel, 50,000 metric tons of copper and 1,600 metric tons of cobalt, including custom feed.
The mill and smelter have been in a planned maintenance shutdown which was scheduled to end today.
